h: חַג הַפֶּסַח, מַאֲמָר נ״ב Pesach — Maamar Nun Bais
Rows of Gold, Studs of Silver: Awe, Love and the Spoils of the Sea

p: תּוֹרֵי זָהָב נַעֲשֶׂה לָּךְ עִם נְקֻדּוֹת הַכָּסֶף
"Rows of gold we will make for you, with studs of silver"
(שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים א', י"א).
(Shir HaShirim 1:11).
בַּמִּדְרָשׁ
In the Midrash
(שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה א', נ"ה):
(Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:55):
"תּוֹרֵי זָהָב" — זוֹ בִּיזַּת הַיָּם, "עִם נְקֻדּוֹת הַכָּסֶף" — זוֹ בִּיזַּת מִצְרָיִם; כְּשֵׁם שֶׁיֵּשׁ הֶפְרֵשׁ בֵּין כֶּסֶף לְזָהָב, כֵּן יֵשׁ שֶׁבַח בִּיזַּת הַיָּם מִבִּיזַּת מִצְרָיִם.

"'Rows of gold'—this is the spoils of the Sea; 'with studs of silver'—this is the spoils of Egypt; just as there is a difference between silver and gold, so is the spoils of the Sea superior to the spoils of Egypt."
וּכְבָר אָמַרְנוּ שֶׁאֵין הַפֵּירוּשׁ עַל כֶּסֶף וְזָהָב, שֶׁזֶּה לֹא הָיָה בְּשׂוֹרָה לְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם: וְאַחֲרֵי כֵן יֵצְאוּ בִּרְכֻשׁ גָּדוֹל

Now we have already explained that this does not refer to physical silver and gold, for that was not the promise given to our father Avraham, peace be upon him, "And afterward they shall go out with great wealth"
(וְנִתְבָּאֵר מַאֲמָר ל"ט),
(as explained in Maamar 39),
רַק הַמְכוּוָן עַל אַהֲבָה וְיִרְאָה, שֶׁנִּקְרָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ הַיִּרְאָה זָהָב וְהַכֶּסֶף חֵשֶׁק וְאַהֲבָה.
rather the intent is love and awe, for in the holy Zohar awe is called gold while yearning and love are called silver.
וְהִנֵּה בְּכָל מָקוֹם אַהֲבָה גְּדוֹלָה מִיִּרְאָה, וְכָאן אָמַר שֶׁגְּדוֹלָה בִּיזַּת הַיָּם שֶׁהוּא זָהָב, יִרְאָה, מִנְּקֻדּוֹת הַכֶּסֶף, אַהֲבָה!
Yet everywhere love is considered greater than fear, whereas here it states that the spoils of the Sea—which is gold, awe—is greater than "studs of silver," love!
גַּם בֶּאֱמֶת זָהָב יָקָר תָּמִיד יוֹתֵר מִכֶּסֶף, וְצָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת לְהֵיפֶךְ, כֵּיוָן שֶׁזָּהָב מְרַמֵּז לְיִרְאָה וְכֶסֶף לְאַהֲבָה!
And indeed, in reality gold is always more precious than silver, which would seem backwards if gold symbolizes awe and silver symbolizes love!
אַךְ כְּתִיב
However, it is written
(דְּבָרִים י', י"ב):
(Devarim 10:12):
מָה ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ שֹׁאֵל מֵעִמָּךְ כִּי אִם לְיִרְאָה
"What does Hashem your God ask of you, except to fear [Him]"

וְהַיְינוּ דִּי"ה מְרַמֵּז לִדְחִילוּ וּרְחִימוּ: דְּיוּ"ד חָכְמָה, וְזֶה בָּא עַל יְדֵי הַחֵשֶׁק וְאַהֲבָה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאוֹמְרִים: אַהֲבַת עוֹלָם בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל עַמְּךָ אָהַבְתָּ, תּוֹרָה וּמִצְוֹת וְכוּלֵּי אוֹתָנוּ לִמַּדְתָּ; ה' בִּינָה לִיבָּא, וְהַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁנִּכְנָס הַיִּרְאָה לְמַעֲמַקֵּי הַלֵּב, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר

meaning that Yud-Hei alludes to fear and love: Yud is Chochmah, which comes through yearning and love, as we say "With an eternal love You have loved Your people the House of Israel; Torah and mitzvos, etc., You have taught us," while Hei is Binah, the inner heart, meaning when awe penetrates into the depths of the heart, as it is said
(Mishlei 2:5):
אָז תָּבִין יִרְאַת ה' וְגוֹמֵר.
"Then you will understand (tavin) the fear of Hashem, etc."
וְכֵן כָּתַב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
And so wrote the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ב' י"ד:):
עֲבִיד לְאַבְרָהָם בְּרָזָא דְּחָכְמָה, לְיִצְחָק בְּרָזָא דִּתְבוּנָה וְכוּלֵּי
"He made Avraham in the secret of Chochmah, and Yitzchak in the secret of Understanding (Tevunah), etc."
וּמִדַּת אַבְרָהָם אַהֲבָה וְיִצְחָק יִרְאָה;
and Avraham's attribute is love while Yitzchak's is awe;
וְכֵן כָּתַב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
and so wrote the holy Zohar
(שָׁם קע"ה:):
(ibid. 175b):
וְחֶסֶד עִילָּאָה נָפְקָא מֵחָכְמָה, גְּבוּרָה דְּהוּא דִּינָא תַּקִּיפָא נָפְקָא מִבִּינָה.
"And Supernal Chessed emerges from Chochmah, while Gevurah, which is rigorous judgment, emerges from Binah."
וְכֵיוָן שֶׁזּוֹכֶה הָאָדָם לְיִרְאָה עִילָּאָה שֶׁנִּכְנָס הַיִּרְאָה לְמַעֲמַקֵּי הַלֵּב, שֶׁהוּא בִּינָה לִיבָּא, זוֹכֶה גַּם כֵּן לְחָכְמָה שֶׁהֵם תְּרֵין רֵעִין דְּלָא מִתְפָּרְשִׁין.

And once a person merits Supernal Awe—when awe penetrates the depths of the heart, which is Binah in the heart—he automatically merits Chochmah as well, for they are two companions that never separate.
וְאוֹתִיּוֹת וָ"ה מְרַמֵּז לְתוֹרָה וּמִצְוֹת, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא
And the letters Vav-Hei allude to Torah and mitzvos, as brought
(רַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא חֵלֶק ג' קכ"ג:):
(Ra'aya Mehemna, Vol. 3, 123b):
הַתּוֹרָה וּמִצְוֹת דְּאִינּוּן בֵּן וּבַת
"Torah and mitzvos, which are Son and Daughter"
וּבְתִיקּוּנֵי זֹהַר
and in Tikkunei Zohar
(תִּיקּוּן כ"א):
(Tikkun 21):

נֵר אִיהִי ה' וְכוּלֵּי, ו' אוֹר הַנֵּר מִלְּגָאו וְכוּלֵּי, וְאוֹר וְנֵר עֲלַיְיהוּ אִיתְּמַר: כִּי נֵר מִצְוָה וְתוֹרָה אוֹר; וְאַמַּאי אִתְחַשְּׁכָן? בְּגִין דְּלָא אִשְׁתַּדְּלָן בְּהוֹן בִּדְחִילוּ וּרְחִימוּ דְּאִינּוּן יָ"ה וְכוּלֵּי, וּמַאן אִילֵּין חֲשׁוֹכִין? סָמֶ"ךְ מֵ"ם וְנָחָשׁ וְכוּלֵּי

"The candle is Hei, etc., Vav is the light of the candle within, etc., and regarding light and candle it is said, 'For a mitzvah is a candle and Torah is light.' And why are they darkened? Because they did not engage in them with fear and love, which are Yud-Hei, etc. And who are these dark forces? Satan and the Serpent, etc."

וְהַיְינוּ סָמֶ"ךְ מֵ"ם וְנוּקְבֵיהּ: סָמֶ"ךְ מֵ"ם שָׂרוֹ שֶׁל עֵשָׂו שֶׁהוּא קְלִיפַּת הַקִּנְאָה, וְהוּא מַחְשִׁיךְ מִדַּת הָאַהֲבָה וְחֶסֶד שֶׁהוּא מִדָּתוֹ שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם, וְנָחָשׁ נוּקְבֵיהּ הוּא קְלִיפַּת הַתַּאֲוָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר

which are Satan and his female counterpart: Satan is the guardian angel of Esav, representing the husk of envy, which darkens the attribute of love and Chessed (Avraham's trait), while the Serpent, his female counterpart, is the husk of lust, as it is said
(Mishlei 5:3):
כִּי חָלָק מִשֶּׁמֶן חִכָּהּ וְגוֹמֵר,
"For her palate is smoother than oil, etc.,"
וְהִיא מַחְשֶׁכֶת הַיִּרְאָה, מִדָּתוֹ שֶׁל יִצְחָק.
and she darkens awe, Yitzchak's trait.
וְעִיקַּר הַשְּׁלֵימוּת שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַתּוֹרָה וּמִצְוָה בִּדְחִילוּ וּרְחִימוּ.
And the essence of perfection is that Torah and mitzvah be performed with fear and love.

וְאִיתָא מֵרַבֵּינוּ רַבִּי בּוּנָם זֵכֶר צַדִּיק לִבְרָכָה לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא דְּעִיקַּר הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת הָאָדָם בְּמִדַּת הַיִּרְאָה, וְאַחַר כָּךְ זוֹכֶה לְאַהֲבָה בְּמַתָּנָה מֵה' יִתְבָּרַךְ, כִּי דַּרְכּוֹ שֶׁל אִישׁ וְכוּלֵּי.

Now it is taught in the name of our master Rabbi Bunim, may the memory of the righteous be a blessing for the life of the World to Come, that man's primary exertion must be in the attribute of awe, and afterward he merits love as a gift from Hashem, may He be blessed, for "it is the way of a man [to pursue, etc.]."

וְהוּא כָּאָמוּר, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי שֶׁזּוֹכֶה לְהַכְנִיס הַיִּרְאָה לְעִמְקֵי לִבּוֹ בִּבְחִינַת בִּינָה לִיבָּא, זוֹכֶה לְחָכְמָה שֶׁהוּא הָאַהֲבָה, דְּחָכְמָה וּבִינָה תְּרֵין רֵעִין דְּלָא מִתְפָּרְשִׁין תָּדִיר.

And this is just as we explained: by meriting to bring awe into the depths of one's heart at the level of Binah in the heart, one automatically merits Chochmah, which is love, because Chochmah and Binah are two inseparable companions.
וְאִיתָא
And it is stated
(שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה כ"א, ח'):
(Shemos Rabbah 21:8):
בִּזְכוּת אַבְרָהָם אֲנִי בּוֹקֵעַ לָהֶם הַיָּם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
"In the merit of Avraham I split the Sea for them, as it is said
(בְּרֵאשִׁית כ"ב, ג'):
(Bereishis 22:3):
וַיְבַקַּע עֲצֵי עֹלָה,
'And he split the wood for the burnt-offering,'
וְאוֹמֵר
and it says
(שְׁמוֹת י"ד, כ"א):
(Shemos 14:21):
וַיִּבָּקְעוּ הַמָּיִם.
'And the waters were split.'"
וְכֵן כָּתַב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
And so wrote the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ב' ק"ע:):
וְאִלְמָלֵא דְּאַשְׁגַּח קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא בִּזְכוּת אַבְרָהָם וְכוּלֵּי כּוּלְּהוּ אִתְאֲבִידוּ בְּיַמָּא וְכוּלֵּי.
"And had the Holy One, blessed is He, not looked upon the merit of Avraham, etc., all of them would have perished in the sea, etc."
וְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
Now it is stated in the holy Zohar
(ibid. 55a):
דְּהָא לֵית פּוּלְחָנָא לְקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא אֶלָּא רְחִימוּתָא וְכוּלֵּי, וְעַל דָּא פּוּלְחָנָא דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא לְרַחֲמָא לֵיהּ בְּכוֹלָּא, כְּמָה דִּכְתִיב
"For there is no service to the Holy One, blessed is He, except love, etc., and therefore the service of the Holy One, blessed is He, is to love Him with everything, as it is written
(דְּבָרִים ו', ה'):
(Devarim 6:5):
וְאָהַבְתָּ אֵת ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ וְכוּלֵּי
'And you shall love Hashem your God, etc.'"
וְאַף דִּכְתִיב: מָה ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ שֹׁאֵל מֵעִמָּךְ כִּי אִם לְיִרְאָה, אַךְ כָּאָמוּר דְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת הָאָדָם בְּיִרְאָה עִילָּאָה, בִּינָה לִיבָּא, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זוֹכֶה לְמִדַּת הָאַהֲבָה.

and even though it is written "What does Hashem your God ask of you, except to fear," nevertheless, as stated, man's exertion is in Supernal Awe (Binah in the heart), and through this he merits the attribute of love.
וְשָׁם בָּעֲקֵידָה כְּתִיב
And there at the Binding of Yitzchak it is written
(בְּרֵאשִׁית כ"ב, י"ב):
(Bereishis 22:12):
כִּי עַתָּה יָדַעְתִּי כִּי יְרֵא אֱלֹהִים אָתָּה וְלֹא חָשַׂכְתָּ וְגוֹמֵר
"For now I know that you are a God-fearing man, and you have not withheld, etc."
וְאַף דְּלִכְאוֹרָה עִנְיַן הָעֲקֵידָה הָיָה מֵרוֹב אַהֲבַת ה' שֶׁדָּחָה אַהֲבַת בְּנוֹ יְחִידוֹ, אַךְ שְׁלֵימוּת הָאַהֲבָה כְּשֶׁבָּא עַל יְדֵי הַיִּרְאָה.

for even though on the surface the Akeidah was motivated by Avraham's overwhelming love of Hashem overriding his love for his only son, nevertheless the perfection of love is specifically when it comes through awe.
וּכְבָר אָמַרְנוּ שֶׁכְּמוֹ שֶׁעַל יְדֵי אַהֲבַת ה' הִשְׁלִיךְ עַצְמוֹ לְכִבְשַׁן הָאֵשׁ—אַף דְּבֶן נֹחַ אֵינוֹ מְצֻוֶּוה עַל קִידּוּשׁ ה'

And we have already explained that just as out of love of Hashem he cast himself into the fiery furnace [of Ur Kasdim]—even though a descendant of Noach is not commanded regarding sanctification of God's Name
(סַנְהֶדְרִין ע"ד:),
(Sanhedrin 74b),
וְאִם כֵּן הָיָה דִּינוֹ יַעֲבוֹר וְאַל יֵהָרֵג, וּלְכַמָּה מֵהָרִאשׁוֹנִים אִם יֵהָרֵג הָוֵי מִתְחַיֵּיב בְּנַפְשׁוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ"ם

so that by strict law he should have transgressed rather than be killed, and according to several early authorities if one gives up his life when exempt he is held accountable for his soul, as the Rambam wrote
(הִלְכוֹת יְסוֹדֵי הַתּוֹרָה פֶּרֶק ה' הֲלָכָה ד'),
(Hilchos Yesodei HaTorah 5:4),
וּבֶן נֹחַ מְצֻוֶּוה שֶׁלֹּא יַהֲרוֹג אֶת עַצְמוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ
and a Noachide is commanded not to take his own life, as they expounded
(סַנְהֶדְרִין נ"ז:):
(Sanhedrin 57b):
שֹׁפֵךְ דַּם הָאָדָם בָּאָדָם,
"'Whoever sheds the blood of man within man'"

וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם הִשְׁלִיךְ עַצְמוֹ לְכִבְשַׁן אֵשׁ, שֶׁאַף שֶׁיְּאַבֵּד עוֹלָמוֹ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם, מִכָּל מָקוֹם מֵרוֹב אַהֲבָתוֹ לַה' מָסַר גַּם נַפְשׁוֹ וְחֶלְקוֹ לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּתְקַדֵּשׁ שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם שֶׁאָדָם מַשְׁלִיךְ עַצְמוֹ לְכִבְשַׁן הָאֵשׁ לְקַדֵּשׁ שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם;

yet nevertheless he cast himself into the fiery furnace, willing even to forfeit his World to Come, God forbid, out of overwhelming love for Hashem, surrendering both his life and his eternal portion so that Heaven's Name be sanctified by a man throwing himself into fire for God's honor;

וְכֵן עַל פִּי מִדַּת אַהֲבָה זוֹ הָיָה צָרִיךְ לַעֲבוֹר עַל מִצְוַת עֲקֵידַת יִצְחָק, כֵּיוָן שֶׁיָּדַע: כִּי בְיִצְחָק יִקָּרֵא לְךָ זָרַע, וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁעַל יָדוֹ יִתְפַּרְסֵם אֱלֹקוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְלֹא רָצָה שֶׁאֱלִיעֶזֶר יִהְיֶה הַמְּפַרְסֵם אֱלֹקוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר: וּבֶן מֶשֶׁק בֵּיתִי הוּא דַּמֶּשֶׂק אֱלִיעֶזֶר

and likewise, following that same logic of love, he would have had to refrain from slaughtering Yitzchak at the Akeidah, knowing that "in Yitzchak shall your seed be called" to publicize God's divinity in the world, not wanting Eliezer to be the one to spread God's Name as he had said "and the steward of my house is Dammesek Eliezer"

אַךְ מִפְּנֵי יִרְאָתוֹ הָעֲצוּמָה לַעֲבוֹר עַל מִצְוַת ה', שֶׁמָּא יֵשׁ לוֹ נְגִיעָה לְאַהֲבַת בְּנוֹ, עַל פִּי מִדַּת הַיִּרְאָה הַזּוֹ עָקַד אֶת יִצְחָק בְּנוֹ, וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: כִּי עַתָּה יָדַעְתִּי כִּי יְרֵא אֱלֹהִים אָתָּה וְלֹא חָשַׂכְתָּ וְגוֹמֵר.

yet because of his immense awe of transgressing Hashem's command—fearing lest his hesitation be tainted by personal love for his son—out of that awe he bound his son Yitzchak, which is why Scripture says "For now I know that you are a God-fearing man, and you have not withheld, etc."
וְאָז נִשְׁלַם בְּמִדַּת הָאַהֲבָה כְּשֶׁבָּא עַל יְדֵי יִרְאָה.
And thus he became perfected in the attribute of love specifically when it came through awe.
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בִּקְרִיעַת יַם סוּף
And this is what is said at the Splitting of the Sea
(שְׁמוֹת י"ד, ל"א):
(Shemos 14:31):
וַיִּירְאוּ הָעָם אֶת ה' וַיַּאֲמִינוּ בַּה'
"And the people feared Hashem and believed in Hashem"
שֶׁאָז זָכוּ לְהַיִּרְאָה עִילָּאָה וֶאֱמוּנָה שְׁלֵימָה, וְזֶהוּ בִּזְכוּת אַבְרָהָם, דִּכְתִיב: וַיְבַקַּע עֲצֵי הָעֹלָה, וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁזָּכוּ לְמִדַּת אַהֲבָה עַל יְדֵי הַיִּרְאָה,

for then they merited Supernal Awe and complete faith—which was in the merit of Avraham, as it is written "And he split the wood for the burnt-offering," meaning they merited the attribute of love through awe
שֶׁהוּא מַה שֶּׁמּוּבָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ: מַאן דְּרָחִים לֵיהּ וְעָבִיד פּוּלְחָנָא בִּרְחִימוּתָא, קָרֵי לֵיהּ קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא רְחִימָא וְכוּלֵּי, רֵעֲךָ וְרֵעַ אָבִיךָ וְכוּלֵּי.
which is what is brought in the holy Zohar, that one who loves Him and serves Him out of love is called by the Holy One, blessed is He, "My beloved, etc., your friend and your father's friend, etc."

וְזֶהוּ: תּוֹרֵי זָהָב נַעֲשֶׂה לָּךְ — זוֹ בִּיזַּת הַיָּם, שֶׁאָז זָכוּ לְיִרְאָה עִילָּאָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וַיִּירְאוּ הָעָם וְגוֹמֵר, שֶׁזֶּהוּ כָּל הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת הָאָדָם: מָה ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ שֹׁאֵל מֵעִמָּךְ כִּי אִם לְיִרְאָה, עִם נְקֻדּוֹת הַכֶּסֶף—שֶׁהוּא בִּיזַּת מִצְרַיִם, שֶׁבָּא מִצַּד הַחֶסֶד וְאַהֲבַת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכוּ לְמִדַּת אַהֲבָה, אַךְ הָיָה רַק לְפִי שָׁעָה וְלָכֵן "נְקֻדּוֹת הַכֶּסֶף" כִּנְקוּדָּה.

And this is "'Rows of gold we will make for you'—this is the spoils of the Sea," when they merited Supernal Awe as it says "And the people feared, etc." (which is man's entire task: "What does Hashem your God ask of you, except to fear"), "with studs of silver"—which is the spoils of Egypt, coming from the kindness and love of the Holy One, blessed is He, for Israel, through which they merited love, yet it was only temporary and therefore "studs of silver" like a fleeting point.
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ה' אִישׁ מִלְחָמָה, ה' שְׁמוֹ—שֶׁאָז זָכוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לְכָל קְדוּשַּׁת שֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה, שֶׁהוּא וָ"ה, תּוֹרָה וּמִצְוֹת, בִּדְחִילוּ וּרְחִימוּ, שֶׁהוּא יָ"ה כָּאָמוּר.

And this is what is meant by "Hashem is a man of war, Hashem is His Name"—for then Israel merited the full holiness of the Name Havayah, which is Vav-Hei (Torah and mitzvos) performed with fear and love (Yud-Hei), as stated.

וְזוֹ הַיִּרְאָה נִמְשְׁלָה לְזָהָב, שֶׁהוּא שְׁלֵימוּת הָאַהֲבָה שֶׁבָּא עַל יְדֵי יִרְאָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּשְׁלַם אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בְּמִדַּת אַהֲבָתוֹ עַל יְדֵי יִרְאָתוֹ הַמּוּפְלֶגֶת בַּעֲקֵידַת יִצְחָק.

And this awe is compared to gold because it is the perfection of love achieved through awe, just as our father Avraham, peace be upon him, was perfected in his attribute of love through his extraordinary awe at the Binding of Yitzchak.
וְזֶהוּ מַה שֶּׁמּוּבָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
And this is what is brought in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק א' קל"ג.):
בְּשַׁעְתָּא דְּעָקִיד לֵיהּ לְיִצְחָק וְכוּלֵּי כְּדֵין אִתְכְּלִיל אֶשָּׁא בְּמַיָּא, וְהַשְׁתָּא אִתְכְּלִילוּ מַיָּא בְּאֶשָּׁא לְמֶהֱוֵי כּוּלָּא רָזָא דִּמְהֵימְנוּתָא עִילָּאָה
"At the moment he bound Yitzchak, etc., then fire [awe] was included in water [love], and now water was included in fire so that all became the secret of Supernal Faith"
וְהוּא כָּאָמוּר, דִּשְׁלֵימוּת הָאַהֲבָה כְּשֶׁבָּא עַל יְדֵי יִרְאָה, וּשְׁלֵימוּת הַיִּרְאָה כְּשֶׁבָּא מֵרוֹב אַהֲבָה,
which is as we explained: the perfection of love is when it comes through awe, and the perfection of awe is when it comes out of overwhelming love,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ תַּנָּא
and as taught in Tanna D'vei Eliyahu
(תַּנָּא דְּבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה פֶּרֶק ג'):
(Tanna D'vei Eliyahu Rabbah, Chapter 3):
אָמַר דָּוִד: אֲנִי יְרֵאתִי מִתּוֹךְ שִׂמְחָתִי וְשָׂמַחְתִּי מִתּוֹךְ יִרְאָתִי, וְאַהֲבָתִי עָלְתָה עַל כּוּלָּם
"David said: 'I feared out of my joy, and I rejoiced out of my fear, and my love surpassed them all'"
וְהַיְינוּ הָאַהֲבָה שֶׁזּוֹכִין עַל יְדֵי יִרְאָה שֶׁמַּכְנִיס לְמַעֲמַקֵּי הַלֵּב, בִּינָה לִיבָּא, וְאָז זוֹכִין לְדַעַת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
which is the love merited through awe that penetrates the depths of the heart (Binah in the heart), whereupon one merits Da'as, as it is said
(Mishlei 2:5):
אָז תָּבִין יִרְאַת ה' וְדַעַת אֱלֹהִים תִּמְצָא
"Then you will understand (tavin) the fear of Hashem, and find the knowledge of God"
שֶׁהוּא שְׁלֵימוּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא
which is the perfection of our father Yaakov, peace be upon him, as brought
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב' י"ד:):
(Zohar, Vol. 2, 14b):
לְיַעֲקֹב בְּרָזָא דְּדַעַת
"to Yaakov in the secret of Da'as"
דְּחִיבּוּר חָכְמָה וּבִינָה מוֹלִיד הַדַּעַת שֶׁהוּא פְּנִימִיּוּת מִכֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן.
for the union of Chochmah and Binah gives birth to Da'as, which is the inwardness of Kesser Elyon.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ
And this is what they said in the Midrash
(שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה כ"א, ח'):
(Shemos Rabbah 21:8):
בִּזְכוּת יַעֲקֹב אֲנִי קוֹרֵעַ לָהֶם אֶת הַיָּם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
"In the merit of Yaakov I split the Sea for them, as it is said
(בְּרֵאשִׁית כ"ח, י"ד):
(Bereishis 28:14):
וּפָרַצְתָּ יָמָּה וְגוֹמֵר.
'And you shall spread out westward (yamah), etc.'"

Just as there is a difference between silver and gold, so the wealth of the Sea is superior to the spoil of Egypt, as it is said, 'And you came with ornament upon ornament.'"

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Dov Ber of Mezritch, Maggid Devarav LeYaakov 32 — “The goal of everything is awe, for if there is no awe, wisdom is not stored up and valued at all, and the goal of wisdom is awe. Although one must serve Hashem, blessed be He, with love and awe, one need take hold only of awe, and of itself the love of the Creator, blessed be He, will rest upon him, for ‘it is the way of a man to pursue’ and so on. A person can test whether his awe is complete: a minister standing before the king, shown the greatest of desires, does not crave it while he stands there.” Connection: The Maggid states the principle Rav Tzadok cites from R. Bunim, that a person works only at awe and love then comes of itself, with the same proof from ‘the way of a man’; he adds that awe can be tested by whether desire falls away.

rich.text: Parallel: R. Dov Ber of Mezritch, Maggid Devarav LeYaakov 32

— “The goal of everything is awe, for if there is no awe, wisdom is not stored up and valued at all, and the goal of wisdom is awe. Although one must serve Hashem, blessed be He, with love and awe, one need take hold only of awe, and of itself the love of the Creator, blessed be He, will rest upon him, for ‘it is the way of a man to pursue’ and so on. A person can test whether his awe is complete: a minister standing before the king, shown the greatest of desires, does not crave it while he stands there.” Connection: The Maggid states the principle Rav Tzadok cites from R. Bunim, that a person works only at awe and love then comes of itself, with the same proof from ‘the way of a man’; he adds that awe can be tested by whether desire falls away.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Parshas Shekalim 1 — “The spoils of the Sea are greater than the spoils of Egypt: at the Exodus they were in the full strength of love for Hashem, and this is ‘studs of silver,’ for silver is love. It is called ‘points’ because it was only for an hour and afterward departed, leaving only a point. At the Splitting of the Sea it says ‘and the people feared Hashem,’ and the attribute of awe is called gold. Though love is greater in its own level, from the side of man’s effort the main thing is awe, as it says ‘except to fear’; for love comes afterward of itself.” Connection: The same reading of gold as awe at the Sea and silver as love in Egypt, with the same reason that awe is man’s part; it adds that ‘points’ marks the love of the Exodus as passing.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Sod Yesharim, Leil Shevi'i shel Pesach 17 — “Nothing remained with man but the yearning from the depth of the heart, and this yearning is called ‘studs of silver.’ And gold denotes awe: through the awe with which a person greatly fears lest this hidden love be concealed from him, he prays and asks Hashem that this love be fixed in his heart like a peg that will never move. Through this fear and awe, those studs of silver, which were scattered, become rows of gold: Hashem makes of these points order and connection, so that the person has a fixed acquisition of this hidden love.” Connection: Both make gold the awe that perfects the love of the Exodus; Sod Yesharim says how: fear of losing the love leads to prayer, and Hashem orders the scattered points of love into fixed rows.
